test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Rays of the Sun converge at a point of 30 cm in front of a concave mirror. Where should the object be placed so that the size of the image is equal to the size of the object?

options.text: Between 30 and 60 cm in front of the mirror
More than 30 cm in front of the mirror
30 cm in front of the mirror
60 cm in front of the mirror

solution:
The object should be placed at a distance of __**60 cm in front of the concave mirror.**__

When rays of light from a distant source like the Sun fall on a concave mirror, they are considered parallel and converge at the **principal focus (F)** of the mirror.

The problem states the rays converge at a point **30 cm** in front of the mirror. Therefore, the **focal length (F)** of the mirror is 30 cm.

For a concave mirror, the image size is **equal** to the object size only when the object is placed at the **Centre of Curvature (C)**

The relationship between the Centre of Curvature and the Focal Length is C = 2f, So C = 2 * 30 = 60 cm.Thus, the object must be placed at the Centre of Curvature, which is 60 cm in front of the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **angle of incidence** is the angle between the incident ray and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• The **angle of refraction** is the angle between the refracted ray and the normal to the surface at the point of refraction.
 
• According to **Snell's Law**, the angle of incidence is not equal to the angle of refraction except in the special case where the two media have the same refractive index.
 
• The refractive index of a medium dictates how much light bends when entering the medium from another medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Snell's Law**

 
 
• It states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
 
• This constant is known as the refractive index.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index**
 
 
• It is a measure of how much the speed of light or other waves is reduced inside a medium compared to a vacuum.
 
• It is given by the formula n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in vacuum and v is the speed of light in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Critical Angle**
 
 
• The critical angle is the angle of incidence above which total internal reflection occurs.
 
• It occurs when light tries to move from a denser medium to a less dense medium.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection**
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
 
• In such cases, the light is completely reflected back into the denser medium.
